I farm 14 mu, so I cannot throw money around, but I also do not dare cut fertilizer too hard. If wheat or maize falls short, that loss is bigger than wasting a little fertilizer. I mostly start from what I did last year and what people around me do here in Quzhou. With well water, I can push yield a bit more steadily than dryland, so I will keep both wheat and maize on the full 14 mu in the wheat-maize cycle. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most of the phosphorus in early, keep nitrogen a bit stronger because wheat here eats fertilizer if I want a full head, and give 3 irrigations if water is normal: once after sowing or before winter if dry, once at jointing, once at grain filling. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what gives better harvest around here, keep nitrogen fairly strong, add some phosphorus and potassium, and give 2 irrigations if rain is not enough, mainly at seedling establishment and around big flare to silking. I do not like risky changes, so I will stay close to the local pattern: wheat with rotary tillage after the maize season, then maize with no-tillage or light direct seeding after wheat harvest to save time. For pests, I will not spray blindly, but I will usually make 2 applications on each crop because one bad outbreak can cost too much grain.
